c1.note: Reuters Oct 20, 2026: Amon told staff in a memo that Qualcomm will cut jobs globally in a performance-focused reduction after annual reviews.

c2.note: The Hindu says the memo was sent Oct 19 and reviewed by Reuters; Reuters says Monday, which is Oct 19.

c3.note: Reuters says notifications are set to begin in November, and later reports confirm cuts began in early November.

c4.note: The memo did not say how many jobs would be affected, and Reuters could not immediately determine the scale.

c5.note: The article says Qualcomm did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

c6.note: India Today: 'Qualcomm declined to comment when contacted by India Today Tech.'

c7.note: No passage was cited for this claim, but India Today reports Qualcomm declined to comment on the cuts; the claim is loosely worded.

c8.note: The Federal says Qualcomm has not officially commented on the India layoffs, and The Hindu says it has not confirmed them.

c9.note: The announcement came through an internal memo reviewed by Reuters, with no public company release found.

c11.note: Moneycontrol, The Federal, India Today and The Hindu all reported on Nov 11 that India layoffs had begun.

c12.note: The Federal says the first round began at Bengaluru on Monday, Nov 9; Moneycontrol says Bengaluru and Hyderabad.

c13.note: Moneycontrol matches this nearly verbatim, citing people familiar, as part of a global restructuring.

c15.note: Investing.com Nov 10: Qualcomm has begun rolling out job cuts affecting India and California, citing people familiar.

c16.note: Investing.com states sources said the cuts are not related to Qualcomm's AI strategy.

c17.note: Investing.com text matches the claim almost verbatim.

c18.note: The Hindu, updated Nov 11, 2026, says more than 1,000 jobs could be at risk in India.

c20.note: India Today on Nov 11, 2026 says Qualcomm has reportedly begun cutting jobs in India, as many as 1,000 employees.

c21.note: Financial Express quotes Pareekh Jain estimating about 1,000 or slightly more India layoffs.

c22.note: Multiple outlets say Qualcomm has not disclosed or confirmed the number or the India layoffs.

c23.note: Reports are sourced to people familiar and analysts; the company has made no announcement or confirmation of totals.

c24.note: Investing.com (Nov 10) says Qualcomm is expected to file California WARN notices in coming days.

c25.note: The 10-K states about 57,000 workers in over 200 locations in 38 countries as of Sept 27, 2026.

c26.note: Reuters says about 52,000 employees as of September last year (2025).

c27.note: Investing.com reports a 26% handset revenue decline in the latest quarterly report.

c31.note: Financial Express and India Today report analysts expect another round of cuts in January; it is an analyst expectation, not company-confirmed.

c32.note: The 7% figure is from press reports and the company has not officially commented or confirmed it; Qualcomm declined comment to India Today.

c33.note: Investing.com says the precise number remains unclear and California WARN counts are unconfirmed, so no final total is established.

c28.note: The 10-K says other expenses in fiscal 2026 consisted of restructuring and restructuring-related charges, substantially all severance costs.

c29.note: The 10-K's other expenses line is $332M for fiscal 2026 (vs $39M), and it consists of the restructuring charges.

c30.note: The 10-K passage gives only a dollar charge and no headcount. I did not read the full filing for headcount, so confidence is medium.

c9.note: Reuters reported on Oct 20, 2026 that the cuts come from an internal memo by CEO Amon that it reviewed. Qualcomm put out no public release and did not respond to Reuters' request for comment.

c21.note: The Federal quotes EIIRTrend's Pareekh Jain saying India 'could account for around 1,000 job losses, or slightly more.' But it cites Financial Express only for the phased rollout, not for Jain's estimate, so the Financial Express attribution is not confirmed. Other outlets put the range at 600–1,200

c23.note: Qualcomm has not confirmed an India total or commented on it. The ~1,000 and 600–1,200 figures come from media reports and analysts, and India Today says the cuts have 'reportedly' begun.
